description: Workflow D error/edge branches from references/alert-subscriptions.md that the happy-path specs do not cover: create against a non-existent sensor (report + do not fabricate a rule), and stop with no matching rule (offer to list + do not DELETE). Both are deterministic and translated to plain language.

expects.query: Deploy the VSS alerts profile on {{platform}} in real-time (VLM) mode using remote LLM and remote VLM endpoints. Then, so later steps have a camera to target, onboard one sensor into VIOS using the vss-manage-video-io-storage skill: upload the bundled warehouse sample video through NVStreamer (port 31000) as a sensor named `warehouse_sample`, then register in VIOS (port 30888) the RTSP URL exactly as NVStreamer's streams API returns it (query NVStreamer for the served URL — do NOT hand-construct a host:port URL, and include BOTH keys in the `/sensor/add` payload — `sensorUrl` (the returned URL) and `name` (`warehouse_sample`); without the `name` key VST silently names the sensor `SENSOR`). Confirm the sensor appears in `GET /sensor/list` with an RTSP stream before finishing. Do NOT finish until the VSS Agent REST API (`curl -sf http://localhost:8000/docs`) and VIOS (`curl -sf http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/sensor/list`) respond successfully and `warehouse_sample` is listed — wait and retry for a few minutes if a service is still starting.
checks: `sh -c 'i=1; while [ "$i" -le 12 ]; do curl -sf --max-time 10 http://localhost:8000/docs >/dev/null 2>&1 && exit 0; sleep 5; i=$((i+1)); done; exit 1'` returns exit 0 (VSS Agent REST API responsive; polls up to ~3 min to absorb deploy readiness timing).
`docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -qx vss-rtvi-vlm` returns exit 0 (continuous VLM processor — required for VLM real-time mode).
`! docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -qx vss-rtvi-cv` returns exit 0 (CV-only perception is NOT running — confirms VLM real-time, not verification).

`sh -c 'i=1; while [ "$i" -le 24 ]; do curl -sf --max-time 10 http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/sensor/list 2>/dev/null | grep -q warehouse_sample && exit 0; sleep 5; i=$((i+1)); done; exit 1'` returns exit 0 (warehouse_sample onboarded into VIOS; polls up to ~2 min to absorb upload/registration delay).

The agent lists VIOS sensors and finds none matching `loading_dock_7`. The route is `vss vios list` (which reads the origin `vss configure` recorded); a direct `GET /vst/api/v1/sensor/list` is also acceptable. What matters is that the agent checked VIOS and concluded the sensor is absent, not which client it used.

Because the sensor does not exist, the trajectory does NOT call Alert Bridge `POST http://localhost:9080/api/v1/realtime` with a fabricated `sensor_id` / `live_stream_url` — the agent does not invent a rule for an unknown sensor.
The agent's final reply states that `loading_dock_7` was not found and lists the available sensor(s) (e.g. `warehouse_sample`) or asks the user to clarify — in plain language, not a raw HTTP error.

expects.query: Stop the fire alert on warehouse_sample.
checks: The agent treats this as a Workflow D stop: it fetches active rules from Alert Bridge (`GET http://localhost:9080/api/v1/realtime`) and filters for a fire-related rule on warehouse_sample.

No matching rule exists, so the agent reports that no matching rule was found for that alert type on warehouse_sample and offers to list what is currently running — it does not fabricate a rule or claim to have stopped one.
The trajectory does NOT issue any `DELETE http://localhost:9080/api/v1/realtime/<id>` — there is nothing to delete and no rule is removed.
